summary: SplitSync iteration 4 backend testing complete. All 76 pytest cases pass in serial mode (21 iter1 + 24 iter2 + 17 iter3 + 14 new iter4). Verified: (1) POST /api/expenses with receipt_image_base64 stores image; response has has_receipt=true and DOES NOT leak receipt_image_base64; GET /api/expenses list shows has_receipt=true and never returns the base64 payload (verified per-item); GET /api/expenses/{id}/receipt returns {image_base64, mime_type} matching the stored base64. (2) POST /api/expenses without receipt -> has_receipt=false; GET /api/expenses/{id}/receipt -> 404 with 'No receipt attached'. (3) GET /api/expenses/unknown/receipt -> 404. (4) GET /api/insights (no month) defaults to current month, returns {month, currency=home, total, count, breakdown:[{category, amount, pct}]} with breakdown sorted desc by amount and pct summing to ~100. (5) GET /api/insights?month=2026-01 groups Jan 2026 expenses by category and converts non-home currencies (EUR->USD verified via live FX). (6) GET /api/insights?month=invalid, 2026-13, 2026-00 all return 400. (7) GET /api/insights without bearer -> 401. (8) Empty month -> count=0, total=0, breakdown=[]. (9) Regressions verified: shares-based split still yields correct per-friend owes, settlements still subtract from shares-derived balances, recurring materialization still creates >=2 weekly items, scan endpoint auth wiring intact.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 843 lines (grew from 773) - well past the 700-line threshold. Should be split into routers (auth, expenses, friends, groups, recurring, settlements, fx, scan, insights), models, and services modules.

insights() re-iterates every expense of the user then filters in Python; better to push month-range filter into the Mongo query using indexed date range (requires ISO string bounds or a proper date field). Fine for current data sizes but will not scale.

insights() calls await convert_amount() inside the async cursor loop per document - each call hits get_rates() lock. Since rates are cached, cost is low, but consider fetching rates once and doing math in memory.

receipt_image_base64 is stored inline in the expenses document. Documents >16MB will fail; typical phone photos base64 can easily reach 5-10MB. Consider GridFS or S3-style external storage with a reference; also add a server-side max-size check on receipt_image_base64.

GET /api/expenses/{id}/receipt hard-codes mime_type='image/jpeg' but POST accepts any base64 (could be PNG/WEBP). Store the mime_type alongside receipt_image_base64 or infer from the base64 magic bytes.
No max-length validation on receipt_image_base64 field in ExpenseCreate. A malicious client could send arbitrarily large payloads.
insights breakdown pct is a raw fraction (float) - could produce many decimals; consider rounding to 2 for API stability. Current tests tolerate ~0.5 pct sum drift.
